Hallo Georg, ich habe hier ohne Zensur die vier besprochenen Szenarien simuliert. Zu jedem Szenario zeige ich die wahre Differenz von Treatment vs. Control (jede Person hat einmal Treatment = 0 und einmal Treatment = 1), die deskriptive Differenz (also wenn man die Daten einfach in Gruppen aufteilt) und die RMST bis zum Zeitpunkt 10 in einem Barchart.

```{r function for descriptive vs true treatment effect, echo = FALSE}
descriptive_vs_true <- function(beta_treatment, treatment_shape_effect){
  
  library(survival)
  library(ggplot2)
  source("Functions/Generate_Data.R")
  
  # simulate big dataset for the same individuals, once with treatment for everyone, once with treatment for no one

  set.seed(1)
  data_all_treatment <- Generate_Data(n = 100000,
                                      p_treat_manual = 1,
                                      beta_treatment = beta_treatment,
                                      treatment_shape_effect = treatment_shape_effect,
                                      censoring = FALSE)

  set.seed(1)
  data_no_treatment <- Generate_Data(n = 100000,
                                    p_treat_manual = 0,
                                    beta_treatment = beta_treatment,
                                    treatment_shape_effect = treatment_shape_effect,
                                    censoring = FALSE)

  data <- rbind(data_all_treatment, data_no_treatment)
  
  # kaplan meier curve
  fit <- survfit(Surv(ObservedTime, Status) ~ Treatment, data = data)
  plot(fit, col = c("red", "blue"), lty = 1:2, xlab = "Time",
       ylab = "Survival Probability", xlim = c(0,20),
       main = "True Treatment difference")
  legend("bottomleft", legend = c("Control", "Treatment"), col = c("red", "blue"), lty = 1:2)
  abline(v = 10)

  data_simulated_normally <- Generate_Data(n = 100000,
                                           beta_treatment = beta_treatment,
                                           treatment_shape_effect = treatment_shape_effect,
                                           censoring = FALSE)
  # kaplan meier curve
  fit <- survfit(Surv(ObservedTime, Status) ~ Treatment, data = data_simulated_normally)
  plot(fit, col = c("red", "blue"), lty = 1:2, xlab = "Time",
       ylab = "Survival Probability", xlim = c(0,20),
       main = "Descriptive Treatment difference")
  legend("bottomleft", legend = c("Control", "Treatment"), col = c("red", "blue"), lty = 1:2)
  abline(v = 10)
  
  # Calculate RMST for both curves
  
  # Compute the Kaplan-Meier curves
  km_fit_all_treatment <- survfit(Surv(ObservedTime, Status) ~ 1, data = data_all_treatment)  # One curve for all individuals
  km_fit_no_treatment <- survfit(Surv(ObservedTime, Status) ~ 1, data = data_no_treatment)  # One curve for all individuals
  
  # Extract RMST at time tau
  RMST_all_treatment <- survival:::survmean(km_fit_all_treatment, rmean=10)[[1]]["rmean"]
  RMST_no_treatment <- survival:::survmean(km_fit_no_treatment, rmean=10)[[1]]["rmean"] 
  
  # Create a data frame for plotting
  df <- data.frame(
    Group = c("Treatment", "Control"),
    RMST = c(RMST_all_treatment, RMST_no_treatment)
  )

  # Plot
  ggplot(df, aes(x = Group, y = RMST, fill = Group)) +
   geom_bar(stat = "identity", width = 0.6) +
   scale_fill_manual(values = c("Treatment" = "blue", "Control" = "red")) +
   labs(y = "RMST", x = "") +
   theme_minimal() +
   theme(legend.position = "none") +
   ggtitle(paste0("RMST difference: ", round(RMST_all_treatment - RMST_no_treatment, digits = 3)))

  
}

```

# Szenarios

```{r}
descriptive_vs_true(beta_treatment = -0.5, treatment_shape_effect = 0) # positive treatment effect, PH holds

```

# Spline Effekt in Szenarios

Für jedes Szenario wird hier ein lineares Modell und ein proportional odds Modell geschätzt. X1-X4 werden mit restricted cubic splines mit 3 Freiheitsgraden transformiert, mit einem zusätzlichen Interaktionseffekt für das treatment.

```{r, echo = FALSE}
rm(list = ls())
library(rms)
source("Functions/Generate_Data.R")
```

```{r function for plotting X1-X4 effects, echo = FALSE}

plot_spline_effects <- function(data, scenario, censoring){
  
  if (!require("rms")) install.packages("rms", dependencies=TRUE)
  
  # Set up datadist (required by rms functions)
  dd <- datadist(data)
  options(datadist = dd)

  # Fit a linear model using restricted cubic splines on X1-X4 with 3 df
  ols_naive <- ols(pseudo ~ X1 + X2 + X3 + X4 + Treatment,
                   data = data)
  ols_spline <- ols(pseudo ~ rcs(X1, 3)*Treatment + rcs(X2, 3)*Treatment +
                    rcs(X3, 3)*Treatment + rcs(X4, 3)*Treatment + Treatment,
                    data = data)

  po_naive <- orm(pseudo ~ X1 + X2 + X3 + X4 + Treatment, data = data)
  po_spline <- orm(pseudo ~ rcs(X1, 3)*Treatment + rcs(X2, 3)*Treatment +
                   rcs(X3, 3)*Treatment + rcs(X4, 3)*Treatment + Treatment,
                   data = data)

  p1 <- plot(Predict(ols_spline, X1, Treatment), main = paste0("GEE X1 effect for scenario ", scenario,
                                                               " with ", censoring, "% censoring" ))
  p2 <- plot(Predict(ols_spline, X2, Treatment), main = paste0("GEE X2 effect for scenario ", scenario,
                                                               " with ", censoring, "% censoring" ))
  p3 <- plot(Predict(ols_spline, X3, Treatment), main = paste0("GEE X3 effect for scenario ", scenario,
                                                               " with ", censoring, "% censoring" ))
  p4 <- plot(Predict(ols_spline, X4, Treatment), main = paste0("GEE X4 effect for scenario ", scenario,
                                                               " with ", censoring, "% censoring" ))
  
  p5 <- plot(Predict(po_spline, X1, Treatment), main = paste0("PO X1 effect for scenario ", scenario,
                                                               " with ", censoring, "% censoring" ))
  p6 <- plot(Predict(po_spline, X2, Treatment), main = paste0("PO X2 effect for scenario ", scenario,
                                                               " with ", censoring, "% censoring" ))
  p7 <- plot(Predict(po_spline, X3, Treatment), main = paste0("PO X3 effect for scenario ", scenario,
                                                               " with ", censoring, "% censoring" ))
  p8 <- plot(Predict(po_spline, X4, Treatment), main = paste0("PO X4 effect for scenario ", scenario,
                                                               " with ", censoring, "% censoring" ))
  
  return(list(p1, p2, p3, p4, p5, p6, p7, p8))
  
}

```

## Bias der Modelle

Für jedes der vier Szenarien wurden je 500 Datensätze mit n=1500 unter drei verschiedenen Zensurstufen (20%, 40%, 60%) simuliert. Die geschätzten ATE-Werte der Modelle wurden mit dem True Treatment-Effekt (True TE) verglichen, um den Bias zu bewerten.

```{r, echo = FALSE}
load("../Output/model_bias_plot.RData")
model_bias_plot
```







## RMSE

```{r, warning=FALSE}
# Loop through the scenarios 1 to 4
for (i in 1:4) {
  # Loop through the censoring levels: 20, 40, 60
  for (j in c(20, 40, 60)) {
    
    # Construct the object name as a string
    obj_name <- paste0("all_plots_", i, "_", j)
    
    # Get object
    obj <- get(obj_name)
    
    p <- obj$RMSE_plot[[1]] + ggtitle(paste("Scenario", i, "Censoring", j, "%"))
    print(p)
    
  }
}    
```




## Estimated Treatment Effect

```{r, warning=FALSE, message = FALSE, fig.height=7, fig.width=6.5}
# Loop through the scenarios 1 to 4
for (i in 1:4) {
  # Loop through the censoring levels: 20, 40, 60
  for (j in c(20, 40, 60)) {
    
    # Construct the object name as a string
    obj_name <- paste0("all_plots_", i, "_", j)
    
    # Get object
    obj <- get(obj_name)
    
    p <- obj$treatment_effect[[1]] + plot_annotation(title = paste("Scenario", i, "Censoring", j, "%"))  
    print(p)
    
    p <- obj$treatment_effect[[2]] + ggtitle(paste("Scenario", i, "Censoring", j, "%"))
    print(p)
    
  }
}    
```
